senses.definition: The width, usually measured in hertz, of a frequency band.

quotes.text: But now is a good time to be bargaining for bandwidth, as the switch from analogue to digital television is freeing up space.
quotes.reference: 2010 October 30, Jim Giles, “Jammed!”, in New Scientist:

senses.definition: (of a signal) The width of the smallest frequency band within which the signal can fit.
(networking, informal) The rate of data flow in digital networks typically measured in bits per second; the bitrate.

quotes.text: While comm buoys allow rapid transmission, there is a finite amount of bandwidth available. Given that trillions of people may be trying to pass a message through a given buoy at any one time, access to the network is parceled out on priority tiers.
quotes.reference: 2008, BioWare, Mass Effect (Science Fiction), Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →ISBN, →OCLC, PC, scene: Communications: Administration Codex entry:

senses.definition: (informal) The capacity, energy or time required.
examples: I think it's a worthy project, but I just don't have the bandwidth right now.

quotes.text: Yet... rather than exploiting opportunities to their fullest, Perry uses with conviction the word "frustrated" to describe a typical approach to government with ideas: "You'll get the response 'we don't have the bandwidth to deal with that'."

quotes.text: Kiriyenko's personal bandwidth to do so is likely limited, however, as he also oversees many of the Kremlin's internal machinations, including the veteran-focused "Time of Heroes" program.

senses.definition: (graph theory) The minimum, over all orderings of vertices of a given graph, of the length of the longest edge.
